entries: Account SID
A Windows security identifier, such as S-1-5-21-...-1001. It names an account, never a person. Who used an account is not shown by the records.
AI-generated draft
Text written by the local language model from finding rows and checked by code. It is triage to help the examiner write the report. It is never evidence.
Allocated / unallocated
Whether the file system still has a live metadata entry for a file. A deleted file is usually unallocated.
Copy first
The drive was copied to a forensic image, the copy was checked against the drive's hash, and the analysis ran on the copy (SWGDE 18-F-001-2.0).
Cross-check disagreement
Two independent parsers read the same record and reported different values. Both values are kept; the examiner decides which is right.
Finding ID
The stable identifier of one row in findings.jsonl, such as F-000123. Every drafted sentence cites the IDs it relies on.
Hardware write blocker
A device between the drive and the computer that stops write commands. AIRLOCK records whether one was used; only blockers with a NIST CFTT test report are recommended.
Hash (SHA-256, MD5)
A fixed-length value computed from data. A different value means different data. The drive is hashed before and after the run.
MFT
The Master File Table of an NTFS volume: one record per file or folder, with names, sizes, and times.
Read directly
The drive was read in place, with no copy kept. This counts as documented triage (SWGDE 17-F-002-2.1).
Recycle bin record
A $I file in $Recycle.Bin that gives the original path, size, and deletion time of a file moved to the recycle bin.
Software read-only policy
AIRLOCK's software settings that keep evidence drives read-only. It is a policy and a second line of defence, not a write blocker.
Time zone basis
utc: recorded in UTC; local_with_offset: local time converted with a known offset; local_unknown_offset: local time, offset unknown, so the time may be off by hours.
Triage
A fast, documented look at a drive to decide what to examine further. Triage results are not a full examination.
USN journal
The NTFS change journal ($UsnJrnl:$J). It records file changes, including deletes, with times. It is often absent on removable media.
Write tracer
AIRLOCK counts write requests that reach the target drive during the run. The expected count is zero.
